newsitem.title: USA: Most school bond issues pass in northern Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Most school bond issues pass in northern Illinois.

text.p: Voters in northeastern Illinois on Tuesday approved seven referendums totaling $229 million of general obligation bond for schools, according to unofficial results from county election offices.
Only two bond referendums, totaling $125.4 million, failed at the polls.

The largest ballot issue was $109.5 million of bonds for Indian Prairie Community School District 204 in the Chicago suburbs of Naperville and Aurora. The issue passed with 6,239 affirmative votes and 2,376 no votes.

A school finance official has said that if the bond referendum passes, the debt would be sold in four issues over four years and that market conditions would dictate whether the deals would sold on a competitive or negotiated basis.
Voters also passed a $40 million bond issue for Cicero School District 99 and a $14 million bond issue for South Berwyn School District 100.

Other bond issues approved by voters were $28 million of bonds for School District 41 and $11 million for School District 89 both in Glen Ellyn. Voters also passed a $20.6 million bond issue for Kaneland School District 302 and a $6 million issue for Cary School District 26.
Voters rejected $45.5 million of bonds for Wheaton-Warrenville School District 200 and a $79.9 million issue for Plainfield School District 202.
